objections.claim: E6 does not make the governed-input mutation the only observable difference. It mandates Bubblewrap `--unshare-net` and `--unshare-pid`, but IPC isolation is a separate `--unshare-ipc` option; private `/dev/shm` does not isolate System V IPC. An input-ignoring oracle can create a System V IPC marker during baseline A, detect and remove it while returning nonzero during B, then observe its absence and return zero during A′—passing the proposed A-B-A′ protocol without inspecting the mutation. This violates the frozen requirement for a discriminating oracle. Require `--unshare-all` (or an explicitly complete namespace set including IPC) and add a System-V-IPC-marker regression that the runner rejects.
